title: ai animation
author: Standard_Buy6885
selftext: it works，What do you think it looks like?

comments.author: No_Surround_4662
comments.body: Is it a rig, or individual sprites? Because one of the answers is good, and one isn't.

replies.author: mlallthethings
replies.body: Curious, what are your answers for rig vs sprite?

replies.author: No_Surround_4662
replies.body:
The level of animation in the image above will be hundreds, if not thousands of sprites for one image - especially at the given frame rate (lots of detail). This kind of rig would be simple, and be 4/5 pngs, or a simple mesh (probably the former though, for this type of animation). 

It's 15kb vs 1-2mb per sprite.

replies.author: Standard_Buy6885
replies.body: You’re right, it’s essentially just a video with a lot of redundant information. But maybe by reducing the number of frames, it could reach a usable level — who knows, people will keep exploring it.

replies.author: No_Surround_4662
replies.body: If you could work on a rigging system that works in the same way controlnet does, I think you’d be onto a winner

replies.author: faen_du_sa
replies.body:
While of course one should explore. But just pratically it dosnt make sense yet.

If you want changes, instead of changing an animation on a rig already in the engine(often can be done in the engine itself, if its a small change), you now have to prompt and hope it dosnt change what you want to keep, while changing what you want. Keep the fidelity the same and pray the AI you use didnt change too much under the hood since last time.

On top of that, in 99% cases its going to take a lot more space/performance then a simple rig with a few pngs. Even if you remove a lot of the frames.

comments.author: DisasterNarrow4949
comments.body: Looks absolutely awesome. What is the workflow?

replies.author: BestFeedback
replies.body: put words in prompt box, press enter, wait.

replies.author: Standard_Buy6885
replies.body: I use ChatGPT-03 to generate the first frame image and prompt, and then create animations with the latest video model (v3 version) from https://jimeng-ai.org/. It’s still not very stable at the moment — I haven’t been able to successfully create close-range combat animations yet, but movement animations are quite stable.
